text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.9% today as crude oil prices dropped sharply, with US crude sliding to $89.53 per barrel. The decline reflects a broader pullback in energy markets and comes on the heels of the UN climate summit's collapse over the weekend—a failure to include fossil fuels in the final deal has fueled concerns about longer-term demand for oil and reinvigorated climate-focused selling pressure on energy stocks.

The stock's slide also fits into a larger unwinding of the refinery trade that Wall Street flagged this week. While geopolitical risks like Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and Iranian tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz would normally support higher oil prices, the market is instead pricing in weaker demand ahead and rotating away from the energy sector broadly.
